Right: "The bus is late." Wrong: "the bus is late"

Right: "The shop opens at 9 o'clock." Wrong: "The shop opens in 9 o'clock."

Hi! Let's ask for things nicely.
I am hungry. I ask: "Can I have an apple, please?"
Rule: ask with "Can I have ... , please?" and not with a bare command.
Right: "Can I have an apple, please?" Wrong: "Give me an apple."

s7039_BASE_o2:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM item=p1]]
Hello! Look at this example. I want to say what I did yesterday. The verb is "see". It is an irregular verb, so its past form is a new word: "saw". I write: "Yesterday I saw a film."
Rule: for a finished event, use the special past form of an irregular verb, with no -ed.
Right: "Yesterday I saw a film." Wrong: "Yesterday I see a film."
Now you try. Write the past form of 'have': Yesterday I ___ a big lunch.

Right: "It is cloudy today." Wrong: "It is cloud today."

Look: I walk to school every day. Yesterday I walked to school. I added -ed because the action is finished.
Rule: for a finished action, add -ed to a regular verb.
Right: "I walked to school yesterday." Wrong: "I walk to school yesterday."
